h1: The 6 Best Countertop Microwaves of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six countertop microwaves compared on capacity, wattage, sensor cooking and price to help you pick the right size.
summary: The TOSHIBA 1.2 cu ft, 1000W model is our best overall pick. The Sharp 2.2 cu ft is the roomiest, the COMFEE the cheap compact choice, the Panasonic NN-SN686S the 1200W pick, and the Farberware adds sensor cooking.
intro: The usual countertop microwave mistake is shopping by cubic feet and ignoring watts. A big cavity with a weak magnetron heats slowly and unevenly, while a small high-wattage unit can feel faster than a larger one rated lower.

We reviewed eight microwaves and kept six with distinct models, ranking them on the spec sheet: capacity, wattage, cooking features and price bucket. Where a listing gave unreliable or unclear numbers, we left them out.

products.name: TOSHIBA Countertop Microwave Oven
products.verdict: A 1.2 cu ft, 1000W microwave that suits most kitchens.
products.description:
The TOSHIBA lists 1.2 cu ft of capacity and 1000W of power in the $100-200 bucket. That is a middle size that fits most countertops and handles dinner plates.

It ranks first because 1000W is a stronger rating than the COMFEE's 700W, and it costs less than the Panasonic and Sharp. It gives up the larger interior of the Sharp and the 1200W of the Panasonic.

It suits couples and small families. The caveat is that the listing names few extra features.
products.idealFor: Couples and small families wanting a balanced size.
products.skipIf: You need to fit large platters.

products.name: Sharp SMC2266KS 2.2 cu. ft. 1200W Stainless Steel Countertop
products.verdict: The biggest cavity here with 1200W behind it.
products.description:
The Sharp SMC2266KS has a 2.2 cu ft interior and 1200W power in stainless steel, in the $200-500 bucket.

It ranks second because it costs more than the TOSHIBA but offers almost double the interior of the COMFEE and more watts than every other pick. The tradeoff is counter space.

It suits big dishes and families. The caveat is the footprint, so measure your counter first.

products.name: Panasonic Microwave Oven NN-SN686S Stainless Steel
products.verdict: 1200W in a 1.2 cu ft stainless body.
products.description:
The Panasonic NN-SN686S is a stainless steel microwave listed at 1.2 cubic feet and 1200W, in the $200-500 bucket.

It ranks third because it matches the TOSHIBA's capacity with 200W more power, though it sits in a higher price bucket. The Sharp offers more space for a similar bucket.

It suits buyers who value speed in a mid-size unit. The caveat is price versus the TOSHIBA.
products.idealFor: Buyers wanting speed in a mid-size unit.

products.name: Farberware 1.6 Cu. Ft. Countertop Microwave Oven
products.verdict: Smart sensor auto cook and defrost at 1100W.
products.description:
The Farberware is a 1.6 cu ft unit at 1100 watts with Smart Sensor Auto Cook settings and defrost, priced $100-200.

Fourth place suits it since the unit sits between the TOSHIBA and Sharp on capacity and watts, and it is the one pick here that lists sensor cooking. That convenience is the main tradeoff for less power than the Sharp.

It suits cooks who reheat and defrost often. The caveat is the thinner brand pedigree.
products.idealFor: Cooks who reheat and defrost often.

products.name: COMFEE' Countertop Microwave Oven
products.verdict: A 0.7 cu ft, 700W unit with an ECO mode, for small spaces.
products.description:
The COMFEE' is a 0.7 cu ft, 700W microwave with an ECO mode, in the $50-100 bucket.

It ranks fifth because its capacity and wattage are the lowest in the list, but it is also the cheapest. Against the TOSHIBA you trade 300W and half a cubic foot for a lower price.

It suits a dorm or office kitchen. The caveat is slower heating.

products.name: Panasonic NN-SN76LS 1.6 cu.ft Cyclonic Inverter Countertop Microwave
products.verdict: A 1.6 cu ft inverter model with listed dimensions.
products.description:
The Panasonic NN-SN76LS is a 1.6 cu ft Cyclonic Inverter microwave measuring 19.44 inches deep, 21.88 inches wide and 11.94 inches high, in the $200-500 bucket.

Sixth place reflects that the listing gives no wattage and the price bucket is higher than the Farberware, which has the same 1.6 cu ft capacity. The inverter design is its draw.

It suits buyers who want to check the footprint precisely. The caveat is the missing wattage.

whatMatters.detail: Wattage is how much power the magnetron delivers, which sets how fast food heats. A 700W unit takes noticeably longer than a 1200W unit. Check the number in the title or bullets rather than assuming.
Cubic feet measures interior volume. A 0.7 cu ft unit may not hold a full dinner plate, while 2.2 cu ft fits large dishes. Compare with the plate you use most.
Sensor cooking adjusts time based on steam, so you do not guess. The Farberware lists it. Look for the words sensor or auto cook in the features.
A bigger interior means a bigger body. Measure counter and cabinet clearance before buying. Look for exterior dimensions, as the Panasonic NN-SN76LS lists.
Stainless steel looks sharper but shows fingerprints. The Sharp and Panasonic NN-SN686S use it. Check finish in the title.

faq.q: What size countertop microwave do I need?
faq.a: The TOSHIBA at 1.2 cu ft suits most households. Go to the Sharp at 2.2 cu ft for large dishes, or the COMFEE' at 0.7 cu ft for a dorm.
Buying by capacity alone. A 1.6 cu ft unit with no listed wattage, like the Panasonic NN-SN76LS, is harder to judge.

faq.q: Is the Sharp worth it over the TOSHIBA?
faq.a: Only if you need a 2.2 cu ft interior and 1200W. Otherwise the TOSHIBA's 1000W is enough.

faq.q: How do I use sensor cooking?
faq.a: Choose the matching auto cook setting and let the microwave sense steam. The Farberware lists Smart Sensor Auto Cook.

faq.q: How do I keep it clean?
faq.a: Wipe the interior after spills and avoid harsh scrubbing. Check the manual for turntable care.
Yes. The COMFEE' at 700W will need more time than the Panasonic NN-SN686S at 1200W.

finalTake: The TOSHIBA at 1.2 cu ft and 1000W is the best pick for most kitchens. Choose the Sharp for large dishes, the Farberware for sensor cooking, or the COMFEE' for tight budgets. Check the wattage in the listing before buying.
